text:
ana: Heads-up: seeing a reproducible coherence drop on rwinf-7b when we enable AWQ with sparse_group=64 + act_quant=true in the canary. coh@20 down ~6% vs FP16 baseline. anyone else?

sam: saw same in staging earlier today, batch/seq pattern looks odd — only appears after warmup. logs show some act-scale spikes.

lee: @ana which canary id and region? :eyes:

ana: canary 37 in dedicated-us-west, serving two routes (chat + summaries). traffic ~0.8rps.

maria: suspect the large sparse_group interacts poorly with activation quant path (FP8 kernel alias). try per_channel_scale=true or reduce group.

sam: quick config we ran locally:
```yaml
model: rwinf-7b
quant_backend: awq
sparse_group: 64
act_quant: true
per_channel_scale: false
batching: dynamic
```
logs snippet:
```
WARN actq: layer 23 scale=1.2e3 overflow_threshold=1.0e3
INFO awq: quantized group=64 latency=18ms
ERROR sample: decode divergence at token 42
```

lee: yep overflow at layer 23. reducing group should lower scale variance. try sparse_group=16 + act_quant=stat-clamp.

ana: tried sparse_group=16 locally — coh@20 drop shrank to ~1.3%, latency +10ms. sample outputs look closer to FP16.

maria: tradeoff expected. smaller groups = more per-group stats = better accuracy but higher compute overhead. we should run a heatmap sweep across group sizes and actq modes (none, stat-clamp, per-channel).

sam: started a quick sweep: groups=[8,16,32,64], actq=[false,stat-clamp,per-channel]. running small eval set (2k prompts) now.

lee: deploy-bot: please start a canary with sparse_group=16 + actq=stat-clamp + kv_warmup=10 for canary 38 in us-west.

deploy-bot: Canary 38 initiated (id=38) — config: sparse_group=16, actq=stat-clamp, per_channel_scale=true, kv_warmup=10. Link: https://deploys.redwood/canaries/38

ana: canary 38 metrics after 45m: coh@20 back within 0.8% of FP16, latency +12ms p50. memory +0.6GB. no obvious decode divergence in sample set.

maria: good. we should snapshot activation heatmaps for the failing layers to compare group effects. asking perf to export layer-scale heatmaps (layer 10-30) for groups 8/16/32/64.

sam: attached sample diffs (excerpt):
"FP16: "The event occurred on April 12..."\nAWQ g64: "Event happened April 12... unrelated sentence"\nAWQ g16: "The event occurred on April 12..."\n"

so g16 matches FP16 better.

lee: plan: 1) finish sweep and aggregate heatmap vs coh tradeoff, 2) run full eval set (10k) for top 2 configs, 3) if g16+stat-clamp passes, promote canary and monitor for 24h, 4) file a postmortem for g64 regression.

ana: created eval run id=2411-awq-sparse-sweep, ETA ~3h. tagging model:rwinf-7b, infra:dedicated-us-west, owner:ana.

maria: also adding a lightweight guard in runtime: if act-scale > 1e3 log at WARN and fall back to per-channel scale for that layer (opt-in). will open PR.

sam: confirming — sweep currently shows g8/g16 best on accuracy, g32 is borderline, g64 fails in tails. latency curve: g8 > g16 > g32 > g64 (g8 slowest).

lee: thanks all. once eval run finishes, let's sync and decide rollout. small note: document all config permutations and full reproduction steps in the bakeoff board.

ana: will update here with final eval numbers. thanks! :thumbsup:
